findings.title: Global view permission bypasses client-specific denials
findings.body: canView(ClientModel) returns true immediately when canView() grants the all-clients VIEW permission, without evaluating permissions on the requested client. Consequently, an administrator granted VIEW on all clients can still view a client with an explicit client-specific denial. This defeats the resource-specific override behavior exercised by the existing user-permission tests. Evaluate the client's effective permission before allowing a global fine-grained grant; only the administrative-role shortcut should bypass that evaluation.

findings.title: Handle existing permission servers without the new Clients resource
findings.body: The fallback assumes getResourceTypeResource() always returns a Clients resource, but realms initialized before this change have only the Users resource. AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when the admin-permissions client already exists, so it never adds the new Clients resource or client-only scopes to those realms. Client permission checks can therefore pass null to findByResource() and subsequently dereference resource.getScopes(), producing server errors instead of an authorization decision. Reconcile existing permission servers with the expanded schema and make this fallback null-safe.
